title: Improved Known-Key Distinguisher for AES*10
summary: A 10-round known-key distinguisher for AES*10 is known, but whether stronger higher-order relations yield a supported improvement remains open.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{AES}^{*}_{10}$, determine whether a stronger higher-order relation than $R8$ could allow deriving several pairs satisfying the differential relation used by the existing 10-round known-key distinguisher and potentially yield a 10-round known-key distinguisher that outperforms that baseline; provide a rigorous proof of the improvement, or, if a rigorous proof is too difficult, a plausible heuristic argument supporting its validity.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of AES*10 using known-key distinguishers and higher-order differential relations.
parameters: R8 — baseline relation to be strengthened
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether a higher-order relation stronger than R8 can yield several relevant differential pairs and an outperforming 10-round known-key distinguisher, supported by a rigorous proof or plausible heuristic argument.

progress.summary: The paper suggests that a relation stronger than R8, yielding several relevant differential pairs, might outperform its 10-round baseline. It leaves the improved distinguisher and a rigorous proof—or plausible heuristic argument—as an open issue.
citation_labels: Henri Gilbert et al., A Simplified Representation of AES
